messages:
ana: proposing we add a compact event_fingerprint (BIGINT) to events_store to help de-dup, cheap sampling, and stable joins across denorm changes. small, deterministic xxhash64 on (tenant_id, route_id, ts, payload_digest) — avoids blowing up PKs

mike: curious about index strategy. if we add a fingerprint and index it we'd get selectivity for backfills, but index bloat risk on writes. what's our write QPS comp here?

ana: typo — ana :) current ingest peaks ~7k req/s for analytics events. sustained ~1.2k. most writes are small, but bursts worry me. thinking of partial index for event_kind in (route, quota_event) to limit bloat.

jin: UI concern — dashboards use event_id + route for dedupe/rollups. if fingerprint changes semantics we need a migration plan for metrics continuity and the alerts pipeline. any read adapters planned?

sam: plan idea: dualwrite adapter in the ingest sidecar that writes to existing schema and new fingerprint column (nullable initially). Start with sidecar that computes fingerprint and writes it. No schema migration downtime.

mike: ok dualwrite is safe. but for historical events we need backfill. full table backfill in PG is expensive. consider shadow table in ClickHouse/OLAP store for fingerprint backfill first and use join for dashboards.

leo: what about a read-side compatibility layer in console that falls back to legacy dedupe if fingerprint is null? So we can roll frontend without waiting for full backfill.

jin: yep, console can implement fallback: if fingerprint IS NULL use (event_id + route) dedupe else use fingerprint. Need a feature flag to opt-in for stricter fingerprint-based dedupe once backfill hits threshold.

ana: propose steps: 1) add nullable fingerprint column + partial index; 2) ship sidecar dualwrite; 3) enable console fallback; 4) backfill elders with sampling + throttle; 5) flip flag once backfill coverage >95%.

mike: SQL sketch for migration:

    ALTER TABLE analytics_events ADD COLUMN event_fingerprint BIGINT NULL;
    CREATE INDEX ON analytics_events (event_fingerprint) WHERE event_kind IN ('route','quota_event');

sam: backfill approach: do staged jobs per tenant windowed by created_at hourly, with consistent chunking by id range. throttle to keep p99 write latency under SLA. We should expose a backfill-progress metric per-tenant.

leo: dashboard mapping: need a short compatibility manifest mapping old-grouping keys -> new fingerprint grouping for existing saved queries. Product can ship a compatibility shim that rewrites queries to use fingerprint when available.

jin: alerts: we must run alerts in parallel against both dedupe methods in canary mode for 48h to compare. Add regression detector: if counts diverge > 0.5% for top 100 metrics, hold rollout.

mike: storage cost estimate: adding BIGINT ~8 bytes * row + index overhead; for 1B rows that's ~8GB plus index. Partial index should keep index size smaller. We'll run a staging simulation.

ana: on the topic of quotas/routing: fingerprint should be stable across replays so quota bookkeeping doesn't double-charge. Hash input must include route_id and tenant_id and canonicalized payload digest. please review hashing spec: xxh64(hex(tenant_id)||"|"||route_sig||payload_digest)

sam: ops-bot scheduled a canary job for migration tests on staging — @ops-bot please post job link when ready.

ops-bot: canary job queued: migration-smoke-1767879999 at https://ci.redwood/migrations/1767879999 (ETA 20m) :white_check_mark:

leo: one more risk: historical queries that rely on event-level uniqueness by event_id may start collapsing differently under fingerprint. we should flag any saved query that uses GROUP BY event_id so product PM can review.

jin: noted. I'll add a migration task to the dashboard saved-query audit: find queries with GROUP BY event_id and tag them for manual review.

mike: also consider creating a lightweight materialized view that precomputes rollups by fingerprint for heavy dashboards — can reduce latency and avoid per-query joins during the backfill window.

ana: timeline request: if we can get dualwrite + console fallback in 2 weeks, backfill over the following month with gradual tenant ramp. sound reasonable?

sam: sounds good. I'll own the dualwrite rollout gating and backfill runner. mike can run cost sim and index bench. jin + leo own console/dashboard fallbacks and saved-query audit.

jin: agreed. starting a doc in #docs/migrations with canary checklist and flags.

ana: thanks team. tagging here: @mike @sam @jin @leo — will follow-up with the hashing spec and a PR for the partial index.

mike: ack. I'll prototype index sizing in staging by replaying a day's write load against the new schema.

ops-bot: canary job completed: migration-smoke-1767879999 ✓ (0 issues found)

leo: nice. I'll queue the saved-query audit and surface top candidates tomorrow.

ana: closing loop — updating roadmap ticket INF-2123 with the plan and owners.
